title: Fundraising: Facilitating electronic offers of securities
subject: This guide addresses the use of email and the internet to make offers of securities under Chapter 6D of the Corporations Act 2001 (Cth). It explains ASIC's interpretation of the fundraising provisions when using electronic disclosure documents and electronic application forms, including their distribution.
background: The guide is issued under the Corporations Act, specifically Chapter 6D, which governs fundraising. It is intended for entities conducting offers of securities electronically, including issuers, AFS licensees, and intermediaries, to clarify compliance obligations and facilitate the use of digital processes.
ruling: ASIC interprets the fundraising provisions to allow electronic disclosure documents and application forms as equivalent to paper-based ones, provided they meet legal requirements such as legibility and accessibility. ASIC has provided relief through legislative instruments, such as ASIC Corporations (Application Form Requirements) Instrument 2017/241, to permit personalised or AFS licensee-created application forms. The guide sets out good practice guidance for electronic distribution, including the use of hypertext links, email, and social media, emphasizing that issuers must ensure documents are not misleading or deceptive. ASIC expects that disclosure documents be easily navigable and that electronic application forms are properly integrated with offer documents. The regulatory approach focuses on ensuring investor protection while embracing technological efficiency.
